# @ternent/identity

> Public identities, private seed capabilities, signatures and Ed25519-to-X25519 derivation.

Published interface baseline: `npm install @ternent/identity@0.6.0-alpha.1`. All functions and types come from the package
root. [Public README](https://github.com/ternent/core/blob/main/packages/identity/README.md).
Installed declarations: `dist/index.d.ts`.

## Capability interface

```ts
import { generateSigner, verifySignature } from "@ternent/identity";
const created = await generateSigner();
if (!created.ok) throw new Error(created.error.code);
const signer = created.value;
const message = new TextEncoder().encode("application.example/v1\0hello");
const signed = await signer.sign(message);
if (!signed.ok) throw new Error(signed.error.code);
const verified = await verifySignature(signer.publicIdentity, message, signed.value);
if (!verified.ok || !verified.value) throw new Error("Invalid signature");
```

`generateSigner()` and `signerFromSeed(seed)` return `PrimitiveResult<BaseIdentityCapability>`.
A seed is exactly 32 private bytes and is copied by the factory. The capability has
`publicIdentity`, exact-byte `sign(message)` and trusted `withX25519Secret(callback)`.
The borrowed scalar is zeroed after the callback settles; do not retain a copy.
Armour's `withAgeDecryption(base)` adds decryption without exporting the seed.

`PublicIdentity` has version 1, algorithm Ed25519, a canonical base64url public key
and its derived identity ID. Validate untrusted identities with `validatePublicIdentity`.
`verifySignature` verifies raw message/signature bytes with strict encoding and point
checks. `ageRecipientFromPublicIdentity` returns a result; `ageRecipientFromSecret`
and `ageSecretKey` encode raw X25519 material. Identity does not encrypt age files.

## Host persistence and recovery

```ts
import {
  createMnemonicIdentity,
  serializeIdentity,
  parseIdentity,
  validateIdentity,
  decodeBase64Url,
  signerFromSeed,
} from "@ternent/identity";
const { identity, mnemonic } = await createMnemonicIdentity({ words: 24 });
const privateExport = serializeIdentity(identity);
const checked = await validateIdentity(parseIdentity(privateExport));
const seed = decodeBase64Url(checked.material.seed);
if (!seed.ok) throw new Error(seed.error.code);
const restored = await signerFromSeed(seed.value);
seed.value.fill(0);
if (!restored.ok) throw new Error(restored.error.code);
```

`SerializedIdentity` contains the private seed; it is not `PublicIdentity` or a
Concord document record. The host protects private exports and recovery phrases.
`parseIdentity` normalizes/checks shape; `validateIdentity` additionally checks
seed/public-key/key-ID consistency. These host helpers throw/reject on invalid input.
The restored base capability signs with the same identity. Armour’s
`withAgeDecryption(restored.value)` adds the decryption operation required by Concord.
Persist the private serialized identity securely; the executable capability itself
is not a portable persistence format.

## Signing conventions and errors

Capability operations return `PrimitiveResult` (`{ ok: true, value }` or
`{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }`). Host mnemonic/serialized helpers throw.
`signBytes`/`signUtf8` and `verifyBytes`/`verifyUtf8` use a context prefix and return/use
base64url signatures. Their default context is `ternent-seal/v2`; select an explicit
context for another application. They are not interchangeable with exact-byte
capability signing. Concord and Ledger construct their own domain-separated messages.
Do not invent an account/profile service or persist secrets inside signed documents.
